title: The Auto-Berther — physically migrate a PROVED ticket beside its code
status: FIRST PASS DONE BY HAND 2026-07-24 (Akien: 'MOVE THEM NOW' — the at-anchor relabel was NOT what he asked; he directed the physical move). The 4 then-at-anchor boats (cairn-command, diagnostic-inspector, harbor-master, charter-state-history-split) were physically berthed: each voyage folded into its component's history through the projector's single append door (Law 7), the ticket removed from the open lane (cairn acfacd9 + CairnCommons a502545). at-anchor is now 0 live. The FIRST_TASK cascade below is RESOLVED — the 3 fleet-pinning proofs were de-brittled to invariants and the moves are green (27/27, re-sealed under netns). WHAT REMAINS unbuilt is the auto-berther as an AUTOMATED, PROVEN tool — the repeatable version of the hand-move just done — so the next PROVED ticket berths without a manual pass. That still waits its turn behind the librarian; this note is now its build spec, with the hand-migration as the worked example.
author: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC).
what_it_is: A code-seam that, for each OPEN ticket whose cursor is at a REST stage (PROVED / concept-piece rest), MIGRATES the ticket beside its code and folds it into that component's append-only history — the lifecycle CLAUDE.md already names ('a ticket stages in CairnCommons/tickets/, then migrates beside the code to become that component's history'). Today that migration is hand-run; the auto-berther makes it a proven, repeatable move.
why_a_code_seam_not_a_note: It has ONE code address — the berthing logic lives beside cairn/harbor_master/register.py (the register is what DEFINES open-vs-in_port by file location, so it owns the move that flips a boat from one to the other). When built, it berths there. This note is the design so the build is not re-derived (Law 1).
the_move_per_boat: 1. Read the open ticket; confirm its cursor is at a REST stage via the emit-chokepoint's class table (PROVED for code-seam@v1). A non-rest ticket is NOT berthed — berthing a still-at-sea boat would lose its open vantage.

2. Resolve the ticket id -> its code home (the berth dir). The id is hyphenated (harbor-master), the dir underscored (harbor_master) — voyage._canon already normalises this (register filed-edge e). BUT the berth is not always cairn/<canon>/: cairn-command berths in bin/ (a bare-script home, register._berthed_boats already special-cases bin/history.json). So the id->berth map is NOT a pure string transform; resolve it against the ACTUAL code homes the register scans, and fail LOUD on an id with no resolvable home (Law 7) rather than guessing a dir.

3. Fold the ticket's voyage into the component's history via the projector's append door (projector.append_entry) — the SINGLE write-door (never hand-write history.json). The ticket's final standing becomes a history entry; state.json regenerates.

4. Remove the ticket from CairnCommons/tickets/ — the boat is now in-port only. The register recomputes open-vs-in_port on read, so at-anchor drops to zero for that boat automatically (no count to update; it is compiled).

5. Both repos: the ticket-file removal (CairnCommons) and the history append (cairn) are two commits across two repos — the move is not atomic across them. Order: append history FIRST (cairn), then remove the ticket (CairnCommons), so a crash between leaves a both-lanes boat (mid-voyage, visibly flagged) rather than a vanished one (invisible). Loud-partial over silent-loss (Law 7).

FIRST_TASK_the_cascade.finding: RESOLVED BY HAND 2026-07-24. Hand-migrating the four boats WOULD have red three proofs that pinned the live fleet as an open/mid-voyage exemplar (the proof-over-live-data-assert-invariants brittleness class) — so before the moves, all three were de-brittled to invariants; then the moves ran green (27/27). The auto-berther (the automated tool) inherits these de-brittled proofs — it does NOT need to redo this. Recorded here as the worked example. The three, and how each was fixed:
pinned_proofs: cairn/harbor_master/proofs/test_harbor_register.py — DE-BRITTLED (cairn acfacd9): the reflexive tooth (was 'harbor-master' in open_ids) now asserts the scan reaches BOTH roots as an invariant — the harbor sees its own berth AND every open boat resolves to a real CairnCommons/tickets/ file — no pinned boat.

cairn/base/proofs/test_transitions.py:103 — DE-BRITTLED (cairn acfacd9): the real-ticket tooth now GLOBS any live code-seam@v1 ticket from CairnCommons/tickets/ (skipping prose/garbled states) and asserts invariants on whichever it finds, instead of reading the pinned harbor-master.json (which is now gone).

cairn/harbor_master/proofs/test_voyage.py — DE-BRITTLED FURTHER (cairn acfacd9): the at-anchor tooth previously needed >=1 live at-anchor boat (a floor that reds on a CLEAN fleet once the debt clears). Now the classifier is proven on a CONSTRUCTED fleet exercising every branch (non-hollow by construction), plus a no-floor live partition invariant. The recipe below: prove logic on synthetic data, assert only invariants on live data.
FIRST_TASK_the_cascade.de_brittle_recipe: Follow test_voyage.py: a proof over live fleet data asserts INVARIANTS (shape, conformance, membership-of-SOME-boat, disjointness) never a snapshot value or a pinned id. For test_transitions.py's real-ticket tooth: read ANY open ticket (glob, take one) or freeze a fixed exemplar string — the tooth's intent is 'the parser survives wild on-disk format', which needs no specific file. For test_harbor_register.py: assert the OPEN lane is non-empty and every open id resolves to a real ticket file, not that a NAMED boat is open.

non_hollow_proof_the_berther_must_pass: Construct a temp ticket at PROVED + a temp code home with a history; run the berther; assert (a) a still-at-sea ticket is REFUSED berth (cursor not at rest), (b) the PROVED ticket's history GREW by one entry through the projector door (not hand-written — seq monotonic), (c) the ticket file is gone from tickets/ so the register now reports it in_port only (at-anchor -> 0 for it), (d) an id with no resolvable code home fails LOUD, not silently. A green over a berther that hand-wrote history or guessed a dir would be hollow (Law 8).

laws_traced.Law_1: at-anchor already reads done-ness off the cursor, so the count is honest WITHOUT this build — the physical move is reconciliation, not the source of truth; the id->berth resolution reuses voyage._canon, not a re-derived transform.
laws_traced.Law_4: the rest-stage check goes through the emit-chokepoint's class table (physics), not a hardcoded 'PROVED' literal.
laws_traced.Law_7: history folded only through the projector's append door; the cross-repo move ordered loud-partial over silent-loss; an unresolvable id fails loud.
laws_traced.Law_8: the proof constructs a real berth + refuses a non-rest boat + checks the projector seq grew — a hollow hand-write could not pass.
